minimum_tls_version.title: Minimum TLS Version
minimum_tls_version.description: The lowest TLS/SSL protocol version the server will accept during handshake negotiation. Versions below TLS 1.2 are associated with known attacks (POODLE, BEAST) and weak cipher suite negotiation paths.

deprecated_versions_explicitly_disabled.title: Deprecated Versions Explicitly Disabled
deprecated_versions_explicitly_disabled.description: Whether SSL 3.0, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1 are explicitly excluded/denied in server configuration rather than simply not listed.

tls_downgrade_protection_enabled.title: TLS Downgrade Protection Enabled
tls_downgrade_protection_enabled.description: Whether the server enforces TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV (RFC 7507) or equivalent downgrade-prevention mechanism to block forced version negotiation to weaker protocols.

allowed_cipher_suites.title: Allowed TLS Cipher Suites
allowed_cipher_suites.description: List of cipher suite identifiers (IANA or OpenSSL names) permitted during TLS negotiation on this endpoint. Also used for forward secrecy analysis.

weak_cipher_suites_explicitly_disabled.title: Weak Cipher Suites Explicitly Disabled
weak_cipher_suites_explicitly_disabled.description: Whether the TLS configuration explicitly excludes weak, export-grade, and NULL cipher suites (RC4, 3DES, EXPORT, NULL, aNULL, eNULL) via deny-list or an approved allowlist that omits them entirely.

forward_secrecy_enforced.title: Forward Secrecy Enforced
forward_secrecy_enforced.description: Whether the TLS configuration explicitly requires ephemeral key exchange (ECDHE or DHE) for all negotiated sessions, preventing non-PFS cipher suites from being selected.

client_certificate_required.title: Client Certificate Required (mTLS)
client_certificate_required.description: Whether the TLS endpoint is configured to require clients to present a valid certificate (mTLS enforcement). True means client certificates are mandatory for session establishment.

client_ca_certificate_configured.title: Client CA Certificate Configured
client_ca_certificate_configured.description: Whether a trusted CA certificate bundle has been configured to validate client certificates. Without this, even if client auth is nominally enabled, certificates cannot be verified.

certificate_chain_validation_enforced.title: Certificate Chain Validation Enforced
certificate_chain_validation_enforced.description: Whether the TLS implementation enforces full certificate chain validation, including trust anchor verification and intermediate CA checks.

hostname_verification_enforced.title: Hostname Verification Enforced
hostname_verification_enforced.description: Whether the TLS layer verifies that the certificate CN or SAN matches the intended hostname of the remote endpoint.

revocation_check_method.title: Certificate Revocation Check Method
revocation_check_method.description: The method used to check certificate revocation status during TLS handshake. A value of 'none' means no revocation checking is performed.

expired_certificates_accepted.title: Expired Certificates Accepted
expired_certificates_accepted.description: Whether the TLS configuration explicitly allows or is known to accept expired certificates without rejection.

session_ticket_rotation_enabled.title: Session Ticket Key Rotation Enabled
session_ticket_rotation_enabled.description: Whether the TLS server rotates session ticket encryption keys on a scheduled basis to limit the window of exposure for captured tickets.

session_ticket_lifetime_seconds.title: Session Ticket Lifetime (Seconds)
session_ticket_lifetime_seconds.description: The maximum lifetime of a TLS session ticket before expiry. Lifetimes exceeding 3600 seconds are generally considered excessive.

session_resumption_mechanism.title: Session Resumption Mechanism
session_resumption_mechanism.description: The TLS session resumption method in use: session tickets (stateless), session IDs (stateful), PSK (pre-shared key for TLS 1.3 0-RTT), or none.

tls_anti_replay_enforced.title: TLS Anti-Replay Protection Enforced
tls_anti_replay_enforced.description: Whether server-side anti-replay protections are enforced for session resumption (e.g., 0-RTT anti-replay checks, single-use session tickets, or nonce tracking).

hsts_header_configured.title: HSTS Header Configured
hsts_header_configured.description: Whether the HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) response header is present and configured with a non-zero max-age on all HTTPS responses.

http_to_https_redirect_enforced.title: HTTP to HTTPS Redirect Enforced
http_to_https_redirect_enforced.description: Whether plain HTTP requests are unconditionally redirected to HTTPS at the server or load balancer level, preventing first-contact cleartext exposure.

app_layer_message_integrity_enabled.title: Application-Layer Message Integrity Enabled
app_layer_message_integrity_enabled.description: Whether individual messages are protected by an application-layer MAC or HMAC signature independent of TLS record-layer integrity (e.g., per-message HMAC, JWS, or signed payload envelopes).

tls_termination_at_proxy.title: TLS Terminated at Intermediate Proxy
tls_termination_at_proxy.description: Whether TLS is terminated at an intermediate proxy (e.g., load balancer, API gateway, reverse proxy) before messages reach the final application endpoint, creating a decrypted transit segment.

tls_connection_rate_limit_enabled.title: TLS Connection Rate Limit Enabled
tls_connection_rate_limit_enabled.description: Whether a rate limit or throttle is applied to incoming TLS session establishment requests (e.g., max new TLS handshakes per second per source IP or globally).

max_concurrent_tls_handshakes.title: Maximum Concurrent TLS Handshakes
max_concurrent_tls_handshakes.description: Configured upper bound on simultaneously in-progress TLS handshakes. A value of 0 indicates no limit is set.

ddos_protection_tier.title: DDoS Protection Tier
ddos_protection_tier.description: Level of active DDoS/volumetric-abuse protection in front of the encrypted endpoint. 'none' means no dedicated protection; 'basic' means default/free-tier only; 'advanced' means paid/configured volumetric protection.

rpki_route_origin_validation_enabled.title: RPKI Route Origin Validation Enabled
rpki_route_origin_validation_enabled.description: Whether RPKI Route Origin Validation is enforced on BGP peers handling traffic to/from the encrypted flow endpoints.

bgp_prefix_filter_policy_applied.title: BGP Prefix Filter Policy Applied
bgp_prefix_filter_policy_applied.description: Whether explicit BGP inbound prefix-list or route-map filters are applied on peering sessions to reject more-specific or unauthorized prefix advertisements for the protected address space.

protected_prefix_max_prefix_length.title: Protected Prefix Maximum Allowed Length
protected_prefix_max_prefix_length.description: The maximum prefix length (in bits) accepted via BGP for the protected address space. More-specific advertisements beyond this length should be rejected to prevent hijacking.

dnssec_validation_enabled.title: DNSSEC Validation Enabled
dnssec_validation_enabled.description: Whether DNSSEC validation is enforced for DNS resolution, preventing spoofed DNS responses from being accepted.

dns_transport_security.title: DNS Transport Security Protocol
dns_transport_security.description: The protocol used to secure DNS queries in transit: none (plaintext UDP/TCP), DoH (DNS-over-HTTPS), or DoT (DNS-over-TLS).

certificate_pinning_enforced.title: Certificate Pinning Enforced
certificate_pinning_enforced.description: Whether the client enforces certificate pinning, preventing acceptance of rogue certificates issued by trusted CAs for the spoofed endpoint.

secure_renegotiation_supported.title: Secure Renegotiation Supported (RFC 5746)
secure_renegotiation_supported.description: Whether the TLS implementation supports and enforces secure renegotiation as defined in RFC 5746, using the renegotiation_info extension or SCSV.

legacy_renegotiation_permitted.title: Legacy (Insecure) Renegotiation Permitted
legacy_renegotiation_permitted.description: Whether the TLS server explicitly allows clients to initiate insecure renegotiation without the RFC 5746 extension. True means unsafe legacy renegotiation is accepted.

client_initiated_renegotiation_allowed.title: Client-Initiated Renegotiation Allowed
client_initiated_renegotiation_allowed.description: Whether the server permits clients to initiate TLS renegotiation. When combined with insecure renegotiation, this enables active MitM injection attacks.

traffic_padding_enabled.title: Traffic Padding Enabled
traffic_padding_enabled.description: Whether the TLS/application layer applies packet padding to normalize packet sizes and obscure payload lengths, mitigating traffic analysis attacks.

traffic_shaping_or_dummy_traffic_enabled.title: Traffic Shaping or Dummy Traffic Enabled
traffic_shaping_or_dummy_traffic_enabled.description: Whether the system injects dummy/cover traffic or enforces constant-rate traffic shaping to mask timing patterns and flow durations from passive observers.
